artefact: decision 985 conformance vectors for `d(x, y)`, and the four-property audit

parent._origin_was_a_parallel_array: `origin` beside `origin_hex`, two lists read positionally. The client found it as a THIRD published convention in one project -- flat `name`/`name_hex`, this parallel pair, and decision 985's nested form -- and a reader has to know which artefact uses which. Retired here in favour of the nested form, so this file carries ONE convention (convention 4: the second copy is what drifts). Their `PublishedBits` already reads all three, so nothing breaks on the retirement.
parent._why_100_m: decision 1004: real 10 m is calibration-only and 100 m is the finest shipped level, so there is no provisional parent here.

format._positions_are_float64_bit_patterns: Every number carries `dec` for readers and `hex` -- the exact IEEE-754 binary64 bits -- for comparison. A conforming implementation reads `hex`; the decimal is not the contract, because a JSON parser's last bits are not a fact anyone has pinned.
format._conditioning_is_given_not_sampled: `slope_deg` and `hand_m` are inputs, not raster lookups. Whether two implementations sample the same layers the same way is a separate question with its own digests and its own cross-repo declaration; this artefact asks only whether two implementations of `d` agree.
format.null_means_nan: `hand_m: null` and `slope_deg: null` are absent values, and their rules differ: absent HAND is FULL amplitude, absent slope is one stratum at full weight.
format._the_node_test_is_in_the_carrier_s_preci: Property 2 is exact against the node positions AS THE CALLER COMPUTES THEM. A consumer whose positions arrive through a single-precision type holds float32(N) for a node N, and float32(N) != N in double -- so a float64 node test never fires for it, and the exactness holds for these vectors while silently failing for everything that draws. A conforming implementation compares the query position against the node position computed and compared in the precision the query arrived in. These vectors are the float64 arm; a float32 carrier must exercise the same rule at its own width, and cannot be checked by float64 positions it cannot represent.

tolerance.derived_from: the spread in `d` when every sine and cosine in it is perturbed by one unit in the last place, over 24 trials at 250 positions
tolerance._why_not_measured_against_the_client: §23.425: a threshold chosen from the number it grades grades nothing. The disagreement between two implementations is what this tolerance EXISTS to bound, so it cannot also be its source.
tolerance.rule: |d_conforming - d_published| <= tolerance_m at every vector, and EXACTLY 0.0 at every vector of class `parent_node`.

float32.finding_1_the_quantum: The client reported 0.125 m and that is the EASTING quantum at this grid's origin. The NORTHING quantum is 0.2500 m -- larger than the finest wavelength the function synthesises (0.1953 m) -- so a single-precision world position cannot address the finest octave on that axis at all, and addresses it at 1.6 samples per wavelength on the other.
float32.finding_2_what_it_costs: Almost nothing, on the surface. An octave ladder falling off at the rows' own exponents puts 3.6e-04 of the field's variance below the float32 Nyquist of 0.50 m, and 1.19e-03 of it below a metre at all. The relief a body sees is the coarsest one or two octaves, and those are addressed at thousands of samples per wavelength. THE CONSTRAINT IS REAL AND THE BILL IS SMALL, and saying only the first half would have sent a client to re-plumb their position type for a few thousandths of a surface.
float32.finding_3_where_it_does_bite: Decision 986 grades the height-difference structure function per stratum, and §23.978 records sub-metre lags against each stratum's fitted law as declared extrapolation. Those lags are answered by exactly the octaves single precision erases. So a float32 carrier's surface is indistinguishable from the reference's to a walker and is not gradeable at all below a metre -- which is a statement about where the conformance check has to run, not about whether the client's rendering is wrong.
float32.consequence_for_this_format: Positions here are float64 bit patterns, never single-precision decimals, because a vector set costs nothing to express exactly and a format that quantises its own inputs cannot later be used to grade the thing it quantised. The `float32_probe` class fails on a carrier that rounds both members of a pair to one position: the point is that the failure is visible, not that the difference it exposes is large.

control_reseeded_world._why: a seed that changes nothing is not a seed; this is the check that the world_seed reaches the arithmetic.

control_half_cell_off_node._why: the instrument must be able to return something other than zero, or 'every node was exactly zero' is a fact about the check.

p3_band_limited.instrument: share of the detail term's variance that survives averaging over one parent cell, debiased for the finite sample per cell

controls._expectation_is: sinc(pi/4)^2 per axis for a one-cell box average, squared for the product of two axes.

p3_band_limited.finding: The construction that buys property 2 injects the energy property 3 forbids, and it is the dominant term rather than a residue. `P[f]` is `f` sampled every 100 m and interpolated back -- but every octave of `f` is at or below half that spacing, so those samples are not a low-pass of `f`, they are an ALIAS of it: independent draws at the parent nodes, Catmull-Rom'd into a smooth random field whose correlation length is the parent's own. Subtracting it does not remove parent-scale energy from `f` (there is almost none to remove) -- it ADDS a parent-scale field of comparable amplitude, which is invented ground at wavelengths §16.5.1 reserves to the fetched data. Measured: 36% of the detail term's variance survives a parent-cell average, against 17% before the subtraction.
p3_band_limited.not_fixed_here: This is a property of the construction §16.5.1 rules, not of this implementation, and the two properties are in genuine tension: a field that is exactly zero on a regular lattice carries lattice-aligned structure somewhere, and the choice is only where to put it. The subtraction spreads it into a smooth random field; the alternatives concentrate it into a visible quilt on the parent grid, which is decision 974's refused seam class arriving through a third channel. Ruling which is owed is the corpus's, not this tool's -- so the number is published and the surface is unchanged.

p4_c1._what_the_control_shows: The linear interpolant keeps property 2 exactly and loses property 4, so the two columns differ in the interpolant and in nothing else. A gap that shrinks with the step is a derivative; one that does not is a corner, and no threshold on the gap itself could have told them apart.

c2_is_absent_and_not_measurable._why: Catmull-Rom is C1 and no more, so `d` has a jump in its second derivative on every parent cell boundary. That jump is roughly 5e-06 per m2 against the field's own 6e-04 -- four orders down -- so a numerical second difference reports the field's curvature and not the jump, at every step size reachable in double precision. Convention 6: the check cannot discriminate, so it says so rather than returning the number it can compute. The absence of C2 is an argument from the interpolant, and the interpolant is not free to change: exactness rests on it being THE SAME one the heightfield uses.

parent_node._what: `d` at parent nodes. EXACTLY 0.0, not within tolerance -- property 2 is the constraint the rest of the function rests on, and a tolerance here would let a conforming implementation lose it silently.

stratum._what: one stratum's own term at its own amplitude, with the HAND taper applied. `slope_deg` is absent because naming a landform bypasses the blend: this is the calibration path 986 grades `S_q(l)` on.

blended._what: the full function: slope chain, margin on HAND, taper. NAN slope and NAN HAND are present on purpose -- absent HAND is full strength and absent slope is one stratum, and both are rules a conforming implementation gets wrong by defaulting the other way.

weight_chain._what: the slope chain driven directly. Its sum is 1 BY CONSTRUCTION -- the telescoping cancels for any ramp shape and any centres -- and asserting that through a world position would test it only at whatever slopes the basin happens to have.
weight_chain.rule: sum of weights == 1.0 within 1e-12; each weight within tolerance

float32_probe._what: pairs of positions closer together than one single-precision step, whose `d` differs. A carrier that rounds both to the same float32 returns the same number twice and FAILS -- which is the constraint being reported rather than rounded away.
float32_probe.rule: both members must be evaluated distinctly; |d_m - reference| <= tolerance_m

_the_top_level_four_are_the_shipped_pare: tolerance, float32, properties and classes above describe the shipped lattice alone. `by_parent` carries every parent the rows reference and is the contract; the four above are the shipped entry of it, repeated for readers that predate the parent axis and due to be dropped once the consumer reads `by_parent`.
